newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama to privatize water plants within a year.
newsitem.headline: Panama to privatize water plants within a year.

text.p: Panama plans to open bids in October to privatize its 48 water plants, a top government official said Wednesday.

"We should be in an advanced stage of the privatization process to open bidding in October with the intention of completing the process by February 1998," National Aqueduct and Sewage System (IDAAN) Executive Director Elida Diaz said.
She said the government had not set an amount it hoped to reap from the sales, adding it was more "concerned with improving service and infrastructure."

Panama will sell 51 percent stock in water plants servicing the nation's two largest cities, Panama City and the Atlantic coast city of Colon, she said. The government will retain 47 percent of stock and workers two percent. Panama will grant concessions of up to 20 years for the remaining water plants.
